references.text: Both verses illustrate biblical naming as a theological affirmation of God's redemptive history in a foreign land.
The verses form a complete narrative arc from naming to the establishment of Ephraim as a symbol of God's blessing for Israel.
Creates a theological contrast between Ephraim's origin as a sign of God's grace in suffering and his later role as an object of God's discipline.
Both verses highlight the theme of God's ability to create fruitfulness and space for His people in foreign or constrained environments.
Creates a powerful theological contrast between Ephraim as a sign of God's grace (Gen 41) and Ephraim as an object of God's wrath (Hos 12).
